NASA just confirmed a massive space telescope plunged into Earth's atmosphere after twenty-two years in orbit. But what if one didn't burn up completely? Most spacecraft vaporize during reentry, but heavy titanium fuel tanks and dense optical mirrors often survive the fiery plunge. Falling at hundreds of miles an hour, an intact piece could smash through roofs and leave a smoking crater in solid ground. Would you keep a piece of space metal if it landed in your yard? Follow for more what-ifs.

Based on today's news: NASA Space Telescope Meets Fiery End After Nearly 22 Years in Orbit - SciTechDaily
